currentContext.strengths: Debt-free balance sheet with investible surplus deployed in mutual fund debt schemes, bank fixed deposits and sovereign bonds|Natural hedge on foreign exchange via exports and import-parity based domestic pricing, supplemented by partial hedging of open FX exposure|Diversified/proactive international sourcing of Styrene Monomer (including China) allowed the Company to avoid major supply constraints to domestic customers despite Strait of Hormuz disruption|Long-standing customer relationships across a large number of small and medium sized customers across all geographical areas, sustained despite short-term availability issues|Entry into automotive-grade compounding (IATF 16949 upgrade at XMold) broadens addressable end-markets beyond appliances
currentContext.strategies: Diversify from core Polystyrene/EPS into ABS and mABS (technology from Versalis, Italy) and Speciality Polymer Compounds to access automotive and appliance compounding demand|Grow the automotive-compounds vertical through subsidiary XMold Polymers (Sri City/Chennai catchment), including SAP integration, grade rationalisation with SPL's range, and upgrading to IATF 16949:2016 including product design capability|Actively promote EPS in insulation and construction pan-India through customer seminars, industry experts and exhibition participation (Plast India, K-Show, REFCOLD, IGBC, BMTPC)|Diversify Styrene Monomer sourcing across international markets (including China) to reduce dependence on any single supply corridor after Middle East disruptions|Fund all capacity expansion from internal accruals, preserving the Company's debt-free balance sheet|Build a circular economy framework around post-consumer EPS/PS plastic waste via education, NGO/ICPE community partnerships and recycling infrastructure, in line with CPCB Extended Producer Responsibility norms|Expand greenfield footprint via a new Munak, Haryana site (land acquisition and environmental clearance in progress)|The Company follows a regular dividend-paying philosophy, confirming an interim dividend already paid during the year and declaring a further final dividend for FY26 at its AGM, indicating shareholder distributions alongside continued reinvestment of profits into capacity-expansion projects.
currentContext.expansion: The Company commissioned the first phase of its 70,000 MTA brown-field mABS project (technology from Versalis, Italy) at the Amdoshi Complex, Maharashtra in September 2025, along with a 20,000 tpa ABS compounding unit (two lines); the mABS plant was shut down in December 2025 due to a critical equipment malfunction and, per corrective advice from Versalis' Italian technical experts, has restarted at a curtailed 65% of installed capacity, targeted to reach 75-80% during the current year. EPS Phase 2 (30,000 MT capacity) was completed and commissioned in April 2026. A second XPS line of 1,50,000 M3 (wide-width capable) has begun construction, targeted for completion by end of FY27. Separately, the Company is developing a new greenfield site at Munak, Haryana, where land acquisition is nearly complete, the pre-project environmental impact assessment is done, environmental clearance is being pursued, and basic infrastructure/site-grading work is planned for the current year. In April 2025 the Company acquired XMold Polymers Pvt. Ltd. (SIPCOT, Gummidipoondi, near Chennai) to build automotive- and appliance-grade compounding capacity for customers in the Sri City AC-manufacturing cluster; post-acquisition, XMold's operations were integrated onto SAP, its engineering-compound grades were rationalised with SPL's range, and its quality system was upgraded to IATF 16949:2016 (including product design under chapter 8.3).

risks.risk: Feedstock (Styrene Monomer) sourcing concentration in the Middle East
risks.note: SM, the Company's main raw material, is largely sourced internationally including from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait; the West Asia war and blockage of the Strait of Hormuz stalled these shipments, forcing reliance on China and other alternate sources and pushing up SM prices sharply in March 2026.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption from the West Asia war impacting exports and supply chains
risks.note: The Company declared force majeure to its export customers after its Middle East SM suppliers declared force majeure; damage to Middle East petrochemical assets is expected to take 4-6 months to normalise post war-end, plus a further 3-4 months for regular shipping availability, delaying export resumption.

risks.risk: Single-plant operational/equipment risk in the new mABS unit
risks.note: The newly commissioned mABS plant at Amdoshi had to be shut down in December 2025 due to malfunction of critical production equipment and is currently running at only 65% of installed capacity, showing execution risk in ramping new capacity.

risks.risk: Import competition and trade-policy risk in Polystyrene
risks.note: Increased cheaper imports from Thailand, Taiwan, Iran and China (as China becomes self-sufficient in PS and Asian exporters redirect to India) are eroding domestic market share; a zero import-duty dispensation on polymer building blocks (in place up to 30 June 2026) would, if extended, further increase competing imports and discourage new domestic capital investment.
The Company has adequately insured its assets against all risks except war risk, leaving asset damage from conflict-related events outside its reinstatement/loss-of-profit insurance cover.

The Company is exposed to dynamic FX rate movements affecting cost and pricing; it only partially hedges open foreign exchange exposure, relying otherwise on a natural hedge from exports and import-parity domestic pricing.

The business depends on secure, always-available IT systems; despite Tier IV data-centre co-location, SOC/NOC monitoring and periodic third-party security audits, the Company explicitly flags data security and system uptime as essential risk areas requiring continuous mitigation.

one-line thesis: Q4FY26 saw strong volume growth and EBITDA margin expansion driven by higher styrene prices and operational efficiency, but full-year profitability was pressured by lower average styrene monomer prices; the key change is the restart of ABS capacity at 65% and commissioning of EPS Phase-II, positioning the company for 8-10% volume growth in FY27 if supply normalizes.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +3% YoY (Q4), -11% YoY (FY26); EBITDA/margin: +17% YoY (Q4), 15.9% margin; EBITDA (total): INR 264cr (Q4), INR 558cr (FY26); PAT (reported): INR 168cr (Q4), INR 327cr (FY26); PAT (normalized): no adjustment disclosed; order book: not disclosed; net debt: INR 0 (debt-free with INR 700cr investable surplus)
guidance: Revenue growth: 8-10% volume growth in FY27 if normalcy returns by June; margin: not specified but expected to improve with volume and stable spreads; order inflow: not quantified; capex/commissioning: INR 250cr total FY27 capex; EPS Phase-II (115ktpa) commissioned April 14, 2026; ABS Phase-II expansion planned for FY28; Haryana project delayed pending IOC SM plant clarity
order book & pipeline: Not disclosed; management indicated no new contracts signed due to fluid pricing, but OEMs are buying on spot basis
segment / subsidiary detail: PS: FY26 volume 363k tons (+2% YoY); EPS: capacity expanded from 85k to 115k tpa; ABS: operating at 65% of 45k tpa (down from 70k tpa design) due to equipment failure; Xmold compounding volume expected to grow 50-60% YoY to 70% utilization; trading sales: 18% of total revenue
growth verticals / optionality: ABS Phase-II expansion (target FY28); EPS export potential to Europe (certified); Xmold expansion into AC OEMs in Sri City; potential de-bottlenecking of PS capacity under evaluation
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA margin improved to 15.9% due to higher volumes and spreads; styrene monomer prices surged from $1,000 to $1,650/ton in March 2026, then moderated to $1,500; spreads for GP PS increased to ~$275/ton from ~$200/ton; non-OEM demand suppressed due to high prices and labor/gas shortages; pass-through to OEMs is partial and spot-based
capex / expansion: FY27 total capex: INR 250cr; EPS Phase-II (INR 115k tpa) commissioned April 2026; ABS Phase-II under planning; Haryana PS/EPS project delayed pending IOC SM plant commissioning; no new capex committed until supply chain stabilizes
capital allocation: Debt-free with INR 700cr surplus; Board recommended final dividend of INR 8/share + interim INR 2.5/share (total INR 10.5/share); all capex funded internally; no M&A or buybacks mentioned
risks & watch-items: Raw material supply disruption from Strait of Hormuz; inventory losses if styrene prices fall; non-OEM demand weakness due to high prices and labor/gas shortages; ABS equipment failure impacting utilization; import competition from Taiwan/Korea (though pricing not yet competitive); delayed IOC SM plant affecting Haryana project
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; management acknowledges volatility and supply chain risks but emphasizes operational resilience, domestic demand focus, and capacity utilization improvements; avoids forward guidance on pricing due to fluidity; confident in long-term demand and import substitution potential
non-obvious takeaways: Internal consumption of 14,000 tons of PS/ABS for compounding is excluded from external sales volumes — this masks true production scale; ABS is not currently used in Xmold compounding despite shared parentage; trading revenue (18%) is material and declining, indicating strategic shift toward value-added manufacturing; inventory levels stable at INR 600cr despite supply crunch, suggesting strategic stockpiling

| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |

| Non-OEM demand suppressed due to high prices and labor/gas shortages | Supreme Petrochem Limited | beneficiary | High | OEMs continue buying despite price hikes, and internal compounding volumes are rising, insulating core business from non-OEM weakness |

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Supreme Petrochem Ltd manufactures Polystyrene (PS), Expandable Polystyrene (EPS), Extruded Polystyrene (XPS), Master Batches, Polymer Compounds and Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS), and also trades Styrene Monomer (SM), its main raw material. The Company operates in the business-to-business (B2B) segment, predominantly serving Original Equipment Manufacturers and a wide spectrum of manufacturing companies across appliance, packaging, automotive and construction-linked end uses, with products reaching customers in 100 countries.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Xmold Polymer Pvt Ltd — subsidiary: Listed as the Company's subsidiary in the Related Party Transactions note; a compounding company acquired to serve automotive/appliance customers.
- The Supreme Industries Limited — related party: Entity having significant influence over the Company (promoter-linked group entity); ordinary-course sale/purchase of goods on commercial/arm's-length basis.
- R. Raheja Investments Private Limited — related party: Entity having significant influence over the Company.
- Exide Industries Ltd — related party: Listed as 'Other Related Party'; Director Rajan B. Raheja also serves as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director on its board.
- Supreme Foundation — related party: Enterprise in which Directors have significant influence; recipient of the Company's CSR donations.
- Society of Rehabilitation of Paraplegics — related party: Enterprise in which Directors have significant influence; recipient of the Company's CSR donations.
- Supreme Petrochem Ltd Employees' Providend Fund Trust — related party: Employee provident fund trust of the Company, classified as an enterprise in which Directors have significant influence.
- PlastIndia International University — related party: Enterprise in which Directors have significant influence; recipient of the Company's CSR donations.

growth_optionality.body: ABS Phase-II expansion (target FY28); EPS export potential to Europe (certified); Xmold expansion into AC OEMs in Sri City; potential de-bottlenecking of PS capacity under evaluation

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- GST rationalisation on air conditioners improved affordability and lifted appliance demand in H2 FY26, expected to continue supporting demand
- PLI-scheme-driven investment scale-up in electronics, mobile phones and air conditioner manufacturing is expected to support downstream polymer demand
- RBI projects India GDP growth of 6.9% in FY27, but the ongoing West Asia war and related supply-chain risk (Middle East dependence for energy/petrochemicals) are flagged as headwinds
- Crude oil prices ruling above US$100/barrel are flagged as a risk to India's import bill, rupee parity and inflation, which could soften demand if sustained
- IMD's forecast of a below-normal South-West monsoon is flagged as a risk to rural demand and inflation
- Zero import duty on most polymer building blocks (in place up to 30 June 2026) is easing input costs but simultaneously increasing competing imports and pressuring domestic industry pricing/investment incentive
- Weak PS demand in FY26 attributed to unseasonal rains/milder summer denting cooling-appliance demand, plus rising cheaper imports from Thailand, Taiwan, Iran and China as Chinese PS capacity redirects exports toward India
- New customer AC-manufacturing capacity investments and commissioning of two large-scale export-oriented AC units in South India are expected to support PS demand from H2 of the current year
- PS market expected to grow marginally (~2.5%) in FY27 with OEM demand growing faster (~5%); EPS Indian market expected to grow ~4%; XPS market expected to grow ~20% in FY27 aided by temperature-sensitive packaging demand
- Non-OEM PS demand may see nil-to-negative growth in the current year due to high product prices, tight working capital and reduced gas availability for polymer processing
- Normalisation of Styrene Monomer supply and export resumption is expected roughly 2-6 months after the West Asia war ends, with regular shipping availability taking a further 3-4 months

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 EBITDA margin improved to 15.9% due to higher volumes and spreads; styrene monomer prices surged from $1,000 to $1,650/ton in March 2026, then moderated to $1,500; spreads for GP PS increased to ~$275/ton from ~$200/ton; non-OEM demand suppressed due to high prices and labor/gas shortages; pass-through to OEMs is partial and spot-based

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company commissioned the first phase of its 70,000 MTA brown-field mABS project (technology from Versalis, Italy) at the Amdoshi Complex, Maharashtra in September 2025, along with a 20,000 tpa ABS compounding unit (two lines); the mABS plant was shut down in December 2025 due to a critical equipment malfunction and, per corrective advice from Versalis' Italian technical experts, has restarted at a curtailed 65% of installed capacity, targeted to reach 75-80% during the current year. EPS Phase 2 (30,000 MT capacity) was completed and commissioned in April 2026. A second XPS line of 1,50,000 M3 (wide-width capable) has begun construction, targeted for completion by end of FY27. Separately, the Company is developing a new greenfield site at Munak, Haryana, where land acquisition is nearly complete, the pre-project environmental impact assessment is done, environmental clearance is being pursued, and basic infrastructure/site-grading work is planned for the current year. In April 2025 the Company acquired XMold Polymers Pvt. Ltd. (SIPCOT, Gummidipoondi, near Chennai) to build automotive- and appliance-grade compounding capacity for customers in the Sri City AC-manufacturing cluster; post-acquisition, XMold's operations were integrated onto SAP, its engineering-compound grades were rationalised with SPL's range, and its quality system was upgraded to IATF 16949:2016 (including product design under chapter 8.3).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Debt-free balance sheet with investible surplus deployed in mutual fund debt schemes, bank fixed deposits and sovereign bonds
- Natural hedge on foreign exchange via exports and import-parity based domestic pricing, supplemented by partial hedging of open FX exposure
- Diversified/proactive international sourcing of Styrene Monomer (including China) allowed the Company to avoid major supply constraints to domestic customers despite Strait of Hormuz disruption
- Long-standing customer relationships across a large number of small and medium sized customers across all geographical areas, sustained despite short-term availability issues
- Entry into automotive-grade compounding (IATF 16949 upgrade at XMold) broadens addressable end-markets beyond appliances

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material supply disruption from Strait of Hormuz; inventory losses if styrene prices fall; non-OEM demand weakness due to high prices and labor/gas shortages; ABS equipment failure impacting utilization; import competition from Taiwan/Korea (though pricing not yet competitive); delayed IOC SM plant affecting Haryana project

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Internal consumption of 14,000 tons of PS/ABS for compounding is excluded from external sales volumes — this masks true production scale; ABS is not currently used in Xmold compounding despite shared parentage; trading revenue (18%) is material and declining, indicating strategic shift toward value-added manufacturing; inventory levels stable at INR 600cr despite supply crunch, suggesting strategic stockpiling

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversify from core Polystyrene/EPS into ABS and mABS (technology from Versalis, Italy) and Speciality Polymer Compounds to access automotive and appliance compounding demand
- Grow the automotive-compounds vertical through subsidiary XMold Polymers (Sri City/Chennai catchment), including SAP integration, grade rationalisation with SPL's range, and upgrading to IATF 16949:2016 including product design capability
- Actively promote EPS in insulation and construction pan-India through customer seminars, industry experts and exhibition participation (Plast India, K-Show, REFCOLD, IGBC, …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-OEM demand suppressed due to high prices and labor/gas shortages | Supreme Petrochem Limited | beneficiary | High | OEMs continue buying despite price hikes, and internal compounding volumes are rising, insulating core business from non-OEM weakness |
| ABS Phase-I operating at 65% capacity due to equipment failure | Supreme Petrochem Limited | beneficiary | Med | Alternate arrangements allow continued production; full capacity restoration and Phase-II expansion remain on track, creating long-term upside |
| Import duty removal on ABS | Taiwan/Korea ABS exporters | loser | Low | Landed price of imported ABS at INR 230/kg still higher than domestic prices, making imports non-competitive despite duty removal |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Company acquired M/S Xmold Polymers Pvt Ltd, a Tier II supplier of polymer compounds to producers of components for automobile companies and appliance manufacturers.
- [Geopolitical supply shock] Closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to war in West Asia stopped all liquid and container cargoes from the Gulf and all three Styrene plants in that region - the company's traditional suppliers - shut operations for safety reasons; SPL established alternate supply arrangements to fulfil the total requirements of all its domestic customers.
- [Exports suspended] Exports were suspended due to non-availability of styrene for exports, significant increase in freight rates, reduced shipping capacity availability and increased voyage time.
- [Spread and pricing] Styrene monomer prices in international markets remained elevated with a brief softening near the end of the June quarter before renewed hostilities pushed them up again; the delta between Styrene monomer and Polystyrene improved significantly in the international market during the quarter, while sharp price increases left demand subdued from non-OEM customers.
- [Import duty] Suspension of import duties on commodity polymer, intended to offset the impact of increased import costs, led to increased imports eating away market share of local producers.
